difficultyReason: Simple two-premise fact stack with a straightforward categorical inference. No nested conditionals or contrapositives required.
stimulus: All members of the orchestra play at least one wind instrument. Sarah is a member of the orchestra.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sarah plays at least one wind instrument.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All wind instrument players are members of the orchestra.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sarah is the best wind instrument player in the orchestra.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most members of the orchestra play wind instruments.

explanations.correct: If all orchestra members play at least one wind instrument, and Sarah is an orchestra member, then Sarah must play at least one wind instrument. This follows directly from the premises.
explanations.A: Overreach — the stimulus says 'at least one,' not 'only' wind instruments. Sarah may play other instruments too.
explanations.B: Correct — logically entailed by the two premises.
explanations.C: Reversal — the stimulus says all orchestra members play wind instruments, not that all wind players are orchestra members.
explanations.D: No information in the stimulus supports any claim about quality or rank.
explanations.E: The stimulus says 'all' orchestra members play wind instruments, not just 'most'.

difficultyReason: Three straightforward declarative facts about a specific event. The correct answer is a simple conjunction of two facts stated in the stimulus.
stimulus: The Rosetta Stone was discovered in Egypt in 1799. The stone contains inscriptions in three languages. Scholars used these inscriptions to decode ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Rosetta Stone is the only artifact ever found that contains multiple languages.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inscriptions in three languages were found on an artifact discovered in Egypt in 1799.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics could not have been decoded before the Rosetta Stone was discovered.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All artifacts discovered in Egypt contain inscriptions in multiple languages.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The three languages on the Rosetta Stone were all spoken in ancient Egypt.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states (1) the Rosetta Stone was discovered in Egypt in 1799, and (2) the stone contains inscriptions in three languages. Combining these two facts yields that inscriptions in three languages were found on an artifact discovered in Egypt in 1799.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus does not say the stone is 'the only' such artifact.
explanations.B: Correct — direct conjunction of facts 1 and 2.
explanations.C: Contradicted by scope — the stimulus says scholars used the stone to decode hieroglyphics, not that it was the only possible means.
explanations.D: Overreach — the stimulus mentions one artifact; no generalization to 'all' artifacts is supported.
explanations.E: Beyond scope — the stimulus does not specify which languages they were or where they were spoken.
